I think people overly complicate talking about emotions by using many different terms for the same feeling, depending on context.

I think this is a pretty exhaustive list of feelings:

  • pleasure (aka happiness, joy, ecstacy, etc)

  • pain (aka sadness, sorrow, loss, hurt, etc)

  • fear (aka jealousy, anxiety, etc): anticipating pain or reduction of pleasure

  • hope (aka excitement, etc): anticipating pleasure or reduction in pain

  • anger (aka hate, rage, etc): a motivating emotion felt towards an object, circumstance, or person that could reduce pleasure or increase pain

I agree with what you're saying except to suggest it "overly" complicates. All those differing words suggest degrees and nuances of the effect upon the psyche for the root emotion. I really like your list of base emotion, but I'm wondering if it's complete.

And finally, I find that the more complicated a language is, the more civilized and unbarbaric the culture using it is. Think about that for a minute. There's a reason I'm a Grammar-Nazi ;-)

I don't think it's bad to have subtly, but so many people I've talked to (particularly other men) don't have a good understanding of their own emotions and would have trouble telling you what they feel. I think more awareness of the basic list would help people be more emotionally intelligent.
